Need a better commit message explaining why this would be a feature that the common pldm stack would need ?

can you please explain "why" ?

I updated the commit message.

This is the reason:
```
The `pldmd` will always create all available PLDM sensors from
terminus PDRs if they include the sensor name and terminus name. But
for pluggable PCIes cards such as NIC card, one PCIe slot can plug the
NIC cards from different manufacture which can have different PDRs set.
This causes the created PLDM sensors names can be different.

But the PLDM sensors can be used by thermal control which should be
independent with the plugged NIC cards. This requires solution to
configure the unique PLDM sensors name for the different OEM PCIe cards
which plugs to the same PCIe slot. This also requires the terminus Name
black list to notify the `pldmd` which terminus it will not
automatically create the PLDM sensors from PRDs.
```

I think Meta also has the same solution which they use the sensor configuration file to create the PLDM sensors for NIC cards. The NIC cards can come from different OEM, but the created sensor name will be unique. So the thermal control can be applied regardless the installed  cards.
In this case, the `pldmd` should not automatically create the PLDM sensors for those cards. and it should not use the sensors name and terminus name from PDRs but the sensor name and terminus name from the configuration file.

I still don't get why we need terminus blacklisting in this case . Thermal control code should ideally look at the PCIe Config space details like the vendor id, subsystem id e.t.c to decide if it's a hot card vs a normal card. The data provided by that card itself (maybe as part of its fru record table) should automatically drive the thermal management code. Why do pldm stack needs to have control ? This stack is supposed to be just acting translator. It should not decide which terminus it should blacklist for thermal control. (may be this logic should be in thermal control code ? perhaps ?)

> I think Meta also has the same solution which they use the sensor configuration file to create the PLDM sensors for NIC cards. The NIC cards can come from different OEM, but the created sensor name will be unique. So the thermal control can be applied regardless the installed  cards.

The thermal control as phosphor-fan-present configuration there is only sensor name https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/5dd0785a7a2d9c3c739331a2e4c2e41bd2423a74/meta-ampere/meta-mitchell/recipes-phosphor/fans/phosphor-fan/groups_2p.json#L97

If we want to unify the fan control algorithm for one platform regardless the Vendor of the installed OCP card we need to unify the created sensor name represent for temperature of OCP card.

What will happen if the OCP card of OEM1 has sensor name in PDR is OCP_Card_Temp and sensorID=10, but the OEM2 as name OCP_Temp and sensor_ID=20? But both sensor report the Card Temp. It is better to use the sensor name in the configuration file in this case.
`Pldmd` will base on the probe condition in FRU to identify the install card is OEM1, then it will create the sensor OCP_Temp and read sensor ID 10 to get card temp.
When pldmd detects the installed card is OEM2, it still create OCP_Temp sensor but the sensorID 20 will be used.

In this case, we need black_list to identify which terminus we will use the name from PDRs which we will use from the sensor configuration file.

> Why do pldm stack needs to have control ? This stack is supposed to be just acting translator. It should not decide which terminus it should blacklist for thermal control. (may be this logic should be in thermal control code ? perhaps ?)

pldm stack does not control the black list for thermal control. It control which terminus it should not use the sensor name from PDRs but from the configuration file.

The pldm-stack spec also mentions that the sensor name can come from EM configuration file.
https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/pldm-stack.md
"pldmd will have the list of $sensorAuxNames from the Terminus's PDRs or the Terminus' EM JSON configuration files". When the terminus has both PDRs and EM sensor configuration, we need the way to chose which name of sensor will come from.
